## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from publisher-disclosed practices (apa.org/pubs/journals/edu, Registered Reports submission guide) gathered 2026-05. Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Medium-High — international education research authorship; cross-cultural learning studies regularly published |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium — accepts non-Western educational data within mainstream educational-psychology framework |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — race, gender, SES, special education papers published with quantitative designs |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Educational psychology + learning sciences — reading/literacy (1,183 articles), achievement/giftedness (820), critical-thinking development (819), early childhood (812), math cognition (792), educational assessments (695) per OpenAlex |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (soft)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **substantive educational psychology contribution** — learning processes, instructional design, achievement outcomes, or assessment methodology. Format-free initial submission (since 2022); APA 7th edition required for revisions.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Resubmission moratorium of 1 year after rejection. Plagiarism check against 40M+ scholarly documents at submission.

### Methodological Preferences

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Core method — RCTs welcomed |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | Accepted with mixed-methods or critical-educational framing |
| Autoethnography | 1 | Rare |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | Accepted when bridging to empirical implications |
| Mixed methods | 4 | Common pattern in educational psychology |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed; PRISMA reporting expected |
| Registered Reports | 5 | Stage 1 → Stage 2 model accepted |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | 1 — APA-style third-person scholarly register |
| **Expected density** | Almost none |
| **Writing style notes** | APA 7th edition for revisions; educational-psychology vocabulary; statistical reporting (effect sizes, multilevel modeling for nested classroom data); Editorial Manager submission platform |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from the educational psychology and learning sciences community — APA Division 15 (Educational Psychology) faculty and senior researchers in learning, assessment, and instructional design. Expect deep literacy in cognitive learning theory, motivation theory, assessment methodology, and modern educational-research methods (multilevel modeling, growth curve modeling, RCT designs). Common reviewer demands: "Educational impact?", "Generalizability across grade levels?", "Methodological rigor for nested data?".

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Educational psychology + learning sciences | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/edu |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Medium |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International educational-psychology programs; APA Division 15 affiliations |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- 1-year resubmission moratorium after rejection (community evidence: APA editorial policy 2026-05)
- Pure qualitative work without educational-psychology framing
- Failure to disclose AI use per APA publisher policy
- Plagiarism flagged via APA's 40M+ document check
- Manuscripts outside educational psychology scope

### Soft Tax

Low for educational-psychology empirical authors. Moderate for cross-disciplinary work — typically requires framing through learning/achievement/instruction lens. Format-free initial submission reduces submission friction; APA 7th edition required only on revision.

### Best Suited For

- Reading and literacy development empirical studies
- Math cognition and achievement research
- Educational assessment methodology
- Innovative teaching and learning method evaluations
- Registered Reports on replication / theory-test work in educational psychology
- Meta-analyses of educational-intervention literatures
- Early childhood and special education research

### Not Recommended For

- Pure autoethnography or first-person teacher narratives
- Critical / decolonial education theory without empirical test (consider qualitative education venues)
- Authors needing rapid turnaround
- Manuscripts framed for non-educational-psychology audiences (consider Journal of Educational Research, Educational Researcher, etc.)

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Developmental Psychology](./developmental-psychology.md) | If the work focuses on developmental processes; APA family |
| 2 | [Journal of Experimental Psychology General](./journal-of-experimental-psychology-general.md) | If the work has general cognitive-experimental angle |
| 3 | *(other educational-research journals — community contribution welcome)* | Authors can also consider Educational Researcher, AERA Open, Learning and Instruction (Elsevier) |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top general-psychology venue as "too applied / too education-focused," J Edu Psych is often a better fit because: it specializes in educational psychology with deep reviewer-pool expertise; learning and achievement frameworks are the journal's native scope; and APA Division 15 affiliation provides built-in audience.
